--help.output: Usage, exit codes and runnable examples.

example.output: Writes authorization.logos and authorization.py in the current directory.
example.dependencies: Writes dependencies.logos and dependencies.py in the current directory.
example.python_prerequisites: Python 3.12+, logos-ai wheel, and the logos executable on PATH.
example.arithmetic: Writes a ready-to-replay addition commutativity proof and an authoring script for six integer identities.

arguments.FILE: UTF-8 proof path or - for standard input

flags.--strict: Require zero used custom axioms after verifying the proof.

success.artifact_sha256: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the checked file bytes
success.statement: verified target proposition tree with declaration IDs
success.custom_axioms: array of {id, statement, statement_text, path} for each used custom axiom, with a checked step path from the target
success.functions: optional array of typed opaque and transparent function declarations

arguments.FILE: UTF-8 proof path or - for standard input

flags.--json: Emit versioned structured proof data for reconstructing the argument.
flags.--markdown: Emit the checked proof as standalone GitHub Markdown with LaTeX math. Mutually exclusive with --json.
flags.--strict: Require zero used custom axioms after verifying the proof.

inspect.success: All check fields plus claim, shared contexts and checked steps in premise-first order.

steps.conclusion: typed proposition tree interpreted in the checked scope
steps.reference_id: custom axiom, checked lemma or core law ID, when applicable
steps.binder: variable display name or hypothesis binder, when applicable
steps.discharged: local assumption step ID, when applicable
steps.context_id: ID of the checked scope shared by this step
steps.binder_sort: sort of the introduced variable or congruence hole, when applicable
steps.introduced_variable: fresh variable ID in the premise scope of forall_intro
steps.introduced_hypothesis: local assumption step ID, when applicable
steps.provenance: {kind, id, proof_step?} for core laws, custom axioms, checked lemmas and local hypotheses
steps.law: {id, formal_statement, substitution: [{formal, actual, sort}]} for a checker-owned law application
steps.substitutions: ordered actual terms for a core law or universal elimination
steps.context: congruence syntax with the substituted term at bound index 0 outside nested binders
steps.premise_conversion: optional {explanation, left, right, common_normal_form} for transitivity
steps.conclusion_conversion: optional {explanation, left, right, common_normal_form} for the verified target or lemma root

inspect.text: Default output prints each checked step with an explanation and premise links.
human_proof_guidance: Use inspect to understand and check the argument.
State the claim and introduce variables and hypotheses in words.
Group routine rewrites into equations and name mathematical laws when useful.
Explain the final conversion naturally and distinguish assumptions from checked lemmas.
Omit internal step IDs, binder IDs, artifact names and hashes from the human proof. Keep the exact trace and identifiers in --json for auditing.
inspect.claim: {statement_field, proof_step, sort}; links the verified target statement to its derivation.
inspect.contexts: Array of {id, variables, hypotheses}. Variables are oldest-first {id, name, sort}; bound index 0 is the last. Hypotheses are active {id, binder, binder_depth} references to local_assumption steps.

exit_codes.3: Valid proof with custom axioms denied by strict policy

proof_format.encoding: UTF-8 JSON, unknown fields and tags rejected
proof_format.bundle: {format, theory, name?, declarations, functions?, custom_axioms, lemmas, target, proof}
proof_format.declaration: {id, name, sort}, sort is prop or int
proof_format.ids: Nonempty strings, unique across declarations, functions, custom axioms and lemmas; core law IDs are reserved
proof_format.lemma: {id, statement, proof}, checked in an empty hypothesis scope when the target proof reaches it

propositions.eq: {tag: eq, left, right}; operands have the same sort
propositions.forall: {tag: forall, name, sort, body}; the body is a proposition

evidence.block: {tag: block, steps, result}; result is a zero-based step index
evidence.step_ref: {tag: step_ref, index}; references an earlier step in the innermost block

proof_format.function: {id, name, params: [sort], result: sort, body?: expression}; transparent bodies can refer to earlier functions

terms.bound: {tag: bound, index}; index 0 denotes the nearest enclosing binder or last parameter
terms.add/sub/mul: {tag, left, right}; both operands are integers
terms.neg: {tag: neg, operand}; operand is an integer
terms.pow: {tag: pow, base, exponent: natural literal}; base is an integer
terms.app: {tag: app, id, args}; arguments have the declared sorts

json_policy_denied.output: Same judgment fields and used axiom paths as default mode. Inspect includes checked steps.
